title: HR Compliance Checklist

HR Compliance Checklist: 7 Key Areas Employers Should Review

HR compliance touches everything from hiring and pay practices to leave, benefits, recordkeeping, and employee policies. In this video, discover seven HR compliance checkpoints employers can review to help identify potential gaps. The video also walks through a simple HR compliance audit built around relevance, consistency, and documentation. For deeper guidance, explore the complete HR compliance guide or explore Paychex HR consulting for personalized HR and compliance support.

Topics:

  • 0:00 - Could Your Business Pass an HR Compliance Check?
  • 0:10 - How Compliance Gaps Usually Start
  • 0:23 - The 7 HR Compliance Checkpoints
  • 2:19 - A Quick Audit You Can Run This Week
  • 2:48 - How Paychex Can Help
  • 3:14 - Wrap Up

<p id="transcript-button">View Transcript</p>

Could Your Business Pass an HR Compliance Check?

0:01 - Could your business pass an HR compliance check today? Most owners think yes. Then they find the gap. And here’s the thing: most businesses don’t get into trouble on purpose. They get there through a missed update, an outdated process, or a document that wasn’t where it should’ve been.

How Compliance Gaps Usually Start

0:20 - So let’s fix that. HR compliance comes down to seven checkpoints. Run through these and you’ve covered much of your risk.

The 7 HR Compliance Checkpoints

0:29 - One: Hiring. Compliance starts before anyone’s hired. Consistent processes, fair candidate evaluation, and EEOC anti-discrimination hired. Consistent processes, fair candidate evaluation, and EEOC anti-discrimination rules protect you — and get you better hires. Two: Wage and hour. Misclassifying an employee as a contractor, or exempt when they’re not, remains one of the most common compliance risks out there. Track time accurately and know the difference. Three: Safety and workplace policies. This is about keeping people safe and setting clear expectations — OSHA duties, harassment prevention, workplace conduct. And document all incidents, because if it’s not documented, it’s hard to prove it happened. Four: Leave and accommodations. FMLA, ADA, paid leave. Handle every request the same way, every time. When the process is clear, employees feel genuinely supported. Five: Benefits and payroll. These are the things employees see every single pay period — payroll taxes, required notices, retirement plans. Get them right and you build real trust. Six: Recordkeeping. If anything’s ever questioned, your files are your defense — payroll records, hiring records, I-9s, performance notes. Keep them complete. Seven: The employee handbook. It ties everything together — policies, leave, pay practices, workplace expectations. And it should reflect how your business actually operates, not how it ran three years ago.

A Quick Audit You Can Run This Week

2:20 - Here’s a fast check you can do this week. Take those seven checkpoints and ask one question of each: is this current, consistent, and documented? That mini-HR compliance audit surfaces most of the gaps hiding in a business.

2:37 - Now, the catch: all seven of these keep changing. Regulations shift; policies age out. That's exactly why businesses are moving away from doing it themselves.

How Paychex Can Help

2:50 - Paychex pairs 50-plus years of HR expertise with AI-powered technology that helps monitor requirements and flag potential gaps before they become costly. Have a question about an employment law? You can get a real-time answer instead of digging through regulations yourself.

3:09 - And when things get complicated, there's a real expert by your side when you need one.

Wrap Up

3:15 - So don’t wait for a gap to find you. Run that quick audit this week and get the full HR compliance guide at the link below. And don’t forget to subscribe for more HR guidance.
